text: If current (I), kinetic energy (K) and charge (Q) are taken as the fundamental quantities, The dimensional representation of power will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Power $P=\dfrac{\text{energy}}{\text{time}}$ and, from $I=\dfrac{Q}{t}$, time $t=\dfrac{Q}{I}$.

$[P]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{K}]}{[\mathrm{Q}][\mathrm{I}]^{-1}}=[\mathrm{K}\mathrm{I}\mathrm{Q}^{-1}]$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Two trucks A and B are approaching each other on a straight path with the velocities of $16\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and $20\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ respectively. When they are $200\mathrm{m}$ apart their drivers see each other and applies the breaks simultaneously. If the truck A decelerates with $2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ and truck B decelerates with $4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, what is the distance between them when they finally stop?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Stopping distance $s=\dfrac{u^{2}}{2a}$.

Truck A: $s_{A}=\dfrac{16^{2}}{2\times 2}=64\mathrm{m}$; truck B: $s_{B}=\dfrac{20^{2}}{2\times 4}=50\mathrm{m}$.

$s_{A}+s_{B}=114\mathrm{m}<200\mathrm{m}$, so they stop without meeting.

Distance between them $=200-114=86\mathrm{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A bullet of mass $10$ gram is fired with velocity of $100\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ from the gun of mass $1\mathrm{kg}$. Recoil speed of the gun is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initial momentum is zero, so by conservation of linear momentum $mv=MV$.

$V=\dfrac{mv}{M}=\dfrac{0.01\times 100}{1}=1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A mass of $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ is attached to one end of a massless spring whose natural length is $1\mathrm{m}$ and spring constant is $800\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$ The other end of the spring is fixed while the mass moves in a circular path in a horizontal plane with an angular speed of $20\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$. The extension in the length of the spring will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The spring force provides the centripetal force; radius of the path $=l_{0}+x$.

$kx=mω^{2}(l_{0}+x)$

$800x=0.5\times 20^{2}(1+x)=200(1+x)$

$600x=200\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The time period of X planet of our solar system is $8$ years. The distance of earth from the sun is $1.5\times 10^{11}\mathrm{m}$. The distance of the X planet from the sun will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Kepler's third law: $T^{2}\propto r^{3}$, with $T_{E}=1$ year.

$r_{X}=r_{E}\left (\dfrac{T_{X}}{T_{E}}\right )^{2/3}=1.5\times 10^{11}\times 8^{2/3}$

$r_{X}=1.5\times 10^{11}\times 4=6\times 10^{11}\mathrm{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
A block of mass M is attached to a wire. The upper part of wire is made of steel and lower part of wire of copper ( as shown in figure ). Both parts have the same area of cross section. Neglecting the mass of wires, the ratio of longitudinal strain developed in steel and copper wires is :

( Given, Young's modulus of steel $=2\times 10^{11}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and Young's modulus of copper $=1.5\times 10^{11}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$ )


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The wires are massless, so the tension in both parts is $Mg$; with equal areas the stress $\dfrac{Mg}{A}$ is the same.

Strain $=\dfrac{\text{stress}}{Y}$, so $\dfrac{ε_{s}}{ε_{c}}=\dfrac{Y_{c}}{Y_{s}}$.

$\dfrac{ε_{s}}{ε_{c}}=\dfrac{1.5\times 10^{11}}{2\times 10^{11}}=\dfrac{3}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: If the r.m.s speed of oxygen at room temperature is $\sqrt{56}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The r.m.s speed of nitrogen at the same temperature is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$v_{rms}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$, so at the same $T$, $v_{rms}\propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$.

$v_{N_{2}}=v_{O_{2}}\sqrt{\dfrac{M_{O_{2}}}{M_{N_{2}}}}=\sqrt{56}\times \sqrt{\dfrac{32}{28}}=\sqrt{64}=8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: An oscillating simple pendulum of time period $T_{o}$ is placed in a lift which is accelerating upwards with $2.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. The time period of pendulum in the lift will be (if $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a lift accelerating upwards, $g_{eff}=g+a=10+2.5=12.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

$T=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g_{eff}}}$, so $\dfrac{T}{T_{o}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{g_{eff}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{10}{12.5}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{4}{5}}$

$T=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}T_{o}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A charge $q$ is uniformly distributed along the length $L$ of a rod. It is then bent in the shape of a semicircle. The magnitude of electric field at the centre of semicircle will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Radius of the semicircle $R=\dfrac{L}{π}$; linear charge density $λ=\dfrac{q}{L}$.

Field at the centre of a uniformly charged semicircular arc: $E=\dfrac{2kλ}{R}=\dfrac{λ}{2π𝜖_{0}R}$

$E=\dfrac{1}{2π𝜖_{0}}\cdot \dfrac{q}{L}\cdot \dfrac{π}{L}=\dfrac{q}{2𝜖_{0}L^{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
In an A.C circuit, V & I are given by $V=250\sin (100t)$ volt and $I=10\sin \left (100t+\dfrac{π}{3}\right )\mathrm{A}$ respectively

The power dissipated in the circuit is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Phase difference $𝜙=\dfrac{π}{3}$.

$P=V_{rms}I_{rms}\cos 𝜙=\dfrac{V_{0}I_{0}}{2}\cos 𝜙$

$P=\dfrac{250\times 10}{2}\times \dfrac{1}{2}=625\mathrm{W}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A plane electromagnetic wave propagating in free space has amplitude of electric field of $900\dfrac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{C}}$. The amplitude of magnetic field will be :$__________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an EM wave in free space, $B_{0}=\dfrac{E_{0}}{c}$.

$B_{0}=\dfrac{900}{3\times 10^{8}}=3\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{T}=3μ\mathrm{T}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Two poloroids $\mathrm{P}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ are placed parallel to each other with common axis.The light of intensity $I_{0}$ passes through a polaroid sheet $\mathrm{P}_{1}$ and then passes through polaroid $\mathrm{P}_{2}$. If $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ is now rotated by $60^{\circ }$, then the intensity of the output light from $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Unpolarised light of intensity $I_{0}$ after $\mathrm{P}_{1}$: $I_{1}=\dfrac{I_{0}}{2}$.

The pass axes are initially parallel; after rotating $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ by $60^{\circ }$, Malus' law gives

$I_{2}=I_{1}\cos ^{2}60^{\circ }=\dfrac{I_{0}}{2}\times \dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{I_{0}}{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A wire of length $8\mathrm{m}$ is bent to form a circular loop in y-z plane. A current of $0.5\mathrm{A}$ is flowing in anticlockwise direction in it, the magnetic dipole moment of the loop is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2πr=8\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{4}{π}\mathrm{m}$; area $A=πr^{2}=\dfrac{16}{π}\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

$m=IA=0.5\times \dfrac{16}{π}=\dfrac{8}{π}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Anticlockwise current in the y-z plane (seen from the $+x$ side) gives a moment along $+\hat{i}$: $⃗{m}=\dfrac{8}{π}\hat{i}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{m}^{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
In the following loop, magnitude of the magnetic field produced at the centre (O) of the loop is : (Assume AB and CD are infinitely extended):


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
O lies on the line of AB, so AB gives no field at O.

CD is a semi-infinite wire with O at perpendicular distance $R$ from its end C: $B_{1}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πR}$, into the page.

The arc BC is three-quarters of a circle carrying current clockwise: $B_{2}=\dfrac{3}{4}\cdot \dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2R}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πR}\cdot \dfrac{3π}{2}$, also into the page.

$B=B_{1}+B_{2}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πR}\left (\dfrac{3}{2}π+1\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Using Boh'r model of quantization of angular momentum the relation between the radius 'r' of the $n^{\text{th}}$ allowed orbit of quantum number 'n' for an electron in hydrogen atom is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Quantisation: $mvr=\dfrac{nh}{2π}$; centripetal condition: $\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}=\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\dfrac{e^{2}}{r^{2}}$.

Eliminating $v$: $r=\dfrac{𝜖_{0}n^{2}h^{2}}{πme^{2}}$

Hence $r\propto n^{2}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron, accelerated through a potential difference of $15056\mathrm{V}$, is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an electron accelerated through $V$ volt, $λ=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}=\dfrac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}$ Å

$\sqrt{15056}\approx 122.7$

$λ=\dfrac{12.27}{122.7}=0.1$ Å

text:
A nuclear physicist performed an experiment on the scattering of alpha particles by thin metal foil of gold. The alpha particles were accelerated up to kinetic energy 3.2 Mev. The estimation of the radius of the nucleus of gold element ($Z=79$) by him is $_______$ $\times 10^{-16}\mathrm{m}$

(Take $\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}\dfrac{\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}^{2}}{\mathrm{C}^{2}}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The estimate is the distance of closest approach: $K=\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}\dfrac{(2e)(Ze)}{r_{0}}$.

$K=3.2\times 10^{6}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}=5.12\times 10^{-13}\mathrm{J}$

$r_{0}=\dfrac{9\times 10^{9}\times 2\times 79\times (1.6\times 10^{-19})^{2}}{5.12\times 10^{-13}}$

$r_{0}=9\times 10^{9}\times 158\times 5\times 10^{-26}=711\times 10^{-16}\mathrm{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A ring is placed at the bottom of a trough containing four immiscible liquids of refractive indices $1.0$, $2.0$, $3.0$ and $4.0$ poured one above the other of heights $10\mathrm{cm}$, $20\mathrm{cm}$, $30\mathrm{cm}$, and $40\mathrm{cm}$ respectively. The apparent depth at which the ring appears, when seen from outside is $__________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For layers viewed normally from air, apparent depth $=\sum \dfrac{t_{i}}{μ_{i}}$.

$=\dfrac{10}{1}+\dfrac{20}{2}+\dfrac{30}{3}+\dfrac{40}{4}=10+10+10+10=40\mathrm{cm}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A sinusoidal voltage $V(t)=200\sin 2000t$ volt is applied to a series LCR circuit in which $L=10\mathrm{mH}$, $C=25μ\mathrm{F}$ and $R=100\Omega$. The impedance of the circuit is $_______$ $\Omega$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ω=2000\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$

$X_{L}=ωL=2000\times 10\times 10^{-3}=20\Omega$

$X_{C}=\dfrac{1}{ωC}=\dfrac{1}{2000\times 25\times 10^{-6}}=20\Omega$

$Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+(X_{L}-X_{C})^{2}}=R=100\Omega$ (resonance)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A cell sends a current through a resistance $4\Omega$ for time $t$ and sends current through another resistance $16\Omega$ for the same time $t$. If the same amount of heat is developed in both the resistances, then the internal resistance of the cell is $_____$ $\Omega$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$H=\left (\dfrac{E}{R+r}\right )^{2}Rt$

$\dfrac{4}{(4+r)^{2}}=\dfrac{16}{(16+r)^{2}}\Rightarrow 16+r=2(4+r)$

$r=8\Omega$ (equivalently $r=\sqrt{R_{1}R_{2}}=\sqrt{4\times 16}$)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
Combination of four parallel plate air capacitors is shown in figure. Separation between the plate $\mathrm{P}_{1}$ & $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ is $\dfrac{d}{3}$ and separation between the plates $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{3}$ is $d$. The equivalent capacitance of the configuration is $_______$ $μ\mathrm{F}$.

(Given $\dfrac{𝜖_{0}A}{d}=4μ\mathrm{F}$. Where A=Area of plates)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Between $\mathrm{P}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ (separation $\dfrac{d}{3}$) three capacitors are in parallel:

$C_{1}=\dfrac{𝜖_{0}(A/6)}{d/3}=2μ\mathrm{F}$, $C_{2}=\dfrac{𝜖_{0}(A/3)}{d/3}=4μ\mathrm{F}$, $C_{3}=\dfrac{𝜖_{0}(A/2)}{d/3}=6μ\mathrm{F}$; sum $=12μ\mathrm{F}$.

Between $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{3}$: $C_{4}=\dfrac{𝜖_{0}A}{d}=4μ\mathrm{F}$, in series with the $12μ\mathrm{F}$.

$C_{eq}=\dfrac{12\times 4}{12+4}=3μ\mathrm{F}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A particle executing SHM has its velocity $20\mathrm{cm}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at mean position and acceleration of $25\mathrm{cm}\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ at one of its extreme position. The amplitude of the particle will be $____ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$v_{\max }=Aω=20$ and $a_{\max }=Aω^{2}=25$

$ω=\dfrac{25}{20}=1.25\mathrm{rad}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

$A=\dfrac{20}{1.25}=16\mathrm{cm}$

text: A water drop of radius $1\mathrm{cm}$ is broken into eight equal droplets. Surface tension of water is $0.075\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. The gain in surface energy is $___________$ $\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$. (Take $π=3.14$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Volume conserved: $8\cdot \dfrac{4}{3}πr^{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}πR^{3}\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{R}{2}=0.5\mathrm{cm}$

$\Delta A=8(4πr^{2})-4πR^{2}=4π(8\times 0.25-1)=4π\mathrm{cm}^{2}=4π\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

$\Delta E=T\Delta A=0.075\times 4\times 3.14\times 10^{-4}=9.42\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{J}$

$\Delta E=942\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{J}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A fly wheel of mass $10\mathrm{kg}$ and radius $50\mathrm{cm}$ is rotating at a rate of $360$ rpm. Assuming mass to be concentrated at the rim, the constant retarding torque required to stop the rotation of wheel in $6$ rotations will be $xπ\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}$. The value of $x$ is $________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass concentrated at the rim: $I=MR^{2}=10\times (0.5)^{2}=2.5\mathrm{kg}\quad \mathrm{m}^{2}$

$ω_{0}=\dfrac{2π\times 360}{60}=12π\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$; $θ=6\times 2π=12π\mathrm{rad}$

$0=ω_{0}^{2}-2αθ\Rightarrow α=\dfrac{(12π)^{2}}{2\times 12π}=6π\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

$τ=Iα=2.5\times 6π=15π\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}\Rightarrow x=15$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: A body moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of $20\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ splits into two parts and continue to move in the same direction . The masses of two parts are in the ratio of $1:2$. The smaller part moves with a speed of $30\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The fractional change is the kinetic energy is given by $\dfrac{1}{x}$. The value of $x$ $is_______$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the parts be $m$ and $2m$. Momentum conservation: $3m\times 20=m\times 30+2mv\Rightarrow v=15\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

$K_{i}=\dfrac{1}{2}(3m)(20)^{2}=600m$

$K_{f}=\dfrac{1}{2}m(30)^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}(2m)(15)^{2}=450m+225m=675m$

$\dfrac{\Delta K}{K_{i}}=\dfrac{75m}{600m}=\dfrac{1}{8}\Rightarrow x=8$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
Two projectiles are thrown towards each other at $15^{\circ }$ and $45^{\circ }$ angles respectively with the horizontal at the same speed. The difference between the horizontal distances traveled by the two projectiles is $80\mathrm{m}$. The initial speed of the projectiles is $______$ $\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

[Given $g=10\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Range $R=\dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g}$.

$R_{45}=\dfrac{u^{2}}{g}$, $R_{15}=\dfrac{u^{2}\sin 30^{\circ }}{g}=\dfrac{u^{2}}{2g}$

$R_{45}-R_{15}=\dfrac{u^{2}}{2g}=80\Rightarrow u^{2}=1600$

$u=40\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift
